items.text: As of 2027, AI agents are moving from writing code to operating infrastructure directly, with humans approving changes rather than authoring every one.
Hyperscaler capital spending, Kubernetes-for-AI adoption, and platform engineering are all accelerating in 2027.
The previous (2026) edition of this Pulumi blog post predicted a cloud-first, AI-driven decade, and those 2026 predictions held up.
Microsoft Azure's revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time in Microsoft's fiscal year 2026 (trailing-year basis).
Google Cloud's backlog reached $514 billion as of Q2 2026.
AWS's AI business exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate as of Q2 2026.
AWS's chips (custom-silicon) business exceeded a $25 billion annualized revenue run rate as of Q2 2026.
According to Gartner (press release 2024-10-23), by 2028 cloud-native platforms will serve as the foundation for more than 95% of new digital initiatives.
According to Gartner, cloud-native platforms served as the foundation for less than 50% of new digital initiatives in 2023.
Gartner (press release 2023-11-29) forecast that worldwide public cloud spending will exceed $1 trillion in 2027.
Gartner described cloud as becoming 'a business necessity' (by 2028), in Gartner's own words.
The 'future of cloud computing' figure (gartner-cloud-2028.png) is credited to Gartner.
McKinsey & Company published a report titled 'In search of cloud value' at the linked mckinsey.com URL.
McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report says cloud value is driven by innovation, which is worth 5x more than cost savings.
McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report projects an EBITDA uplift of 20–30% by 2030 for high-performing organizations.
McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report says Asia leads in projected cloud value, followed by the US and Europe.

McKinsey's 'In search of cloud value' report says high-ROI organizations excel by aligning cloud strategy with business priorities, building strong cloud foundations, and using modern operating models.
Teams succeeding in the cloud transition increasingly use infrastructure as code, automation, and unified governance frameworks like Pulumi Insights + Policies.
Hyperscalers are currently making the largest infrastructure investments in cloud history, nearly all centered on AI workloads, inference, and high-performance compute.
AWS's Q2 2026 revenue growth was its fastest since 2021.
AWS revenue was $42.2 billion in Q2 2026 (per Amazon's Q2 2026 earnings release).
AWS revenue grew 37% year-over-year in Q2 2026 (per Amazon's Q2 2026 earnings release).
AWS revenue grew 28% year-over-year in Q1 2026, the quarter before Q2 2026.
AWS's chips business includes its custom Trainium and Graviton silicon.
AWS's AI business and its chips business were each growing at triple-digit percentages year-over-year as of Q2 2026.
Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 ended June 30, 2026, and the Azure $100 billion milestone was reported in results published 2026-07-29.
Azure revenue grew 43% year-over-year in Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026.
Azure revenue grew 40% year-over-year in Microsoft's fiscal Q3 2026, the quarter prior to fiscal Q4 2026.
Satya Nadella said, verbatim: 'This year, Azure revenue surpassed $100 billion for the first time' (Microsoft fiscal Q4 2026 results, 2026-07-29).
Satya Nadella is Microsoft's chairman and CEO.
Google Cloud revenue rose 82% year-over-year in Q2 2026.
Google Cloud revenue was $24.8 billion in Q2 2026.
Google Cloud's backlog was $106 billion in Q2 2025, a year before it reached $514 billion.
Alphabet raised its full-year 2026 capital expenditure guidance to $195–205 billion at its Q2 2026 earnings call.
Alphabet's prior full-year 2026 capex guidance, before the Q2 2026 raise, was $180–190 billion.
Alphabet's $180–190 billion 2026 capex estimate had itself already been raised twice during 2026 before the Q2 2026 raise.
Oracle reported FY2026 cloud revenue of $34.0 billion.
Oracle's FY2026 cloud revenue was up 39% year-over-year.
Oracle's remaining performance obligations reached $638 billion at the end of FY2026 (per Oracle's Q4/FY2026 results release).
Oracle's remaining performance obligations were up 363% year-over-year at the end of FY2026.
Oracle attributed its FY2026 RPO growth to large-scale AI infrastructure contracts, including prepaid and customer-supplied GPU deals totaling $75 billion.
The pages https://www.pulumi.com/aws/#video ('deploy AWS infrastructure at the speed of AI with Pulumi') and https://www.pulumi.com/docs/insights/policy/ (Pulumi Policies) exist.
Hybrid and multi-cloud strategies are now mainstream.
ResearchAndMarkets (via BusinessWire, 2025-05-13) forecasts the hybrid cloud market will grow from $130 billion to $310–330 billion by 2030.
Mordor Intelligence's hybrid cloud market report says 87% of enterprises run workloads across multiple clouds.
Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprises will adopt hybrid compute architectures in mission-critical workflows by 2028, up from 8%.
Pulumi's 2026 State of Agentic Infrastructure survey (pulumi.com/state-of-agentic-infrastructure/) surveyed 510 platform, DevOps, and product engineers.
Pulumi's 2026 survey found 64% of surveyed teams run on AWS.
Pulumi's 2026 survey found 55% of surveyed teams run on Google Cloud.
Pulumi's 2026 survey found 45% of surveyed teams run on Azure.
Pulumi's 2026 survey found most surveyed teams run on more than one cloud, i.e., multi-cloud is already the norm among respondents.
The 'most popular cloud computing infrastructure by industry' figure is credited to Cloud Worldwide Service / Forbes.
Modern cloud teams use infrastructure as code, reusable components/internal platforms, and policy-driven guardrails for multi-cloud operation.

Pulumi provides a multi-cloud IaC model, Pulumi Policies, and internal developer platform capabilities (linked at pulumi.com/docs/iac/, /product/insights-governance#video, /product/internal-developer-platforms/#video).
Organizations are currently moving beyond AI prototypes and integrating AI into core products, internal workflows, and customer-facing systems.
Gartner (press release 2026-05-19) forecasts total worldwide AI spending across software, hardware, and services to reach $2.59 trillion in 2026.
Gartner forecasts worldwide AI spending in 2026 to be a 47% increase year-over-year.
IDC (FutureScape 2026) predicts that by 2027 half of enterprises will be using AI agents to redefine how humans and machines collaborate.

Enterprises are investing in GPU provisioning/orchestration, model-serving infrastructure, identity/secrets/access controls, IaC automation, and policy-driven governance, and are increasingly using software engineering approaches to standardize AI infrastructure.

Pulumi's Superintelligence Infrastructure page (pulumi.com/product/superintelligence-infrastructure/) explains why AI workloads from pre-training to inference require dynamic infrastructure orchestration rather than static configuration.
Pulumi IaC is used for standardized AI infrastructure.
Pulumi ESC manages secrets and configuration at scale, centralizing and governing credentials, keys, and tokens.
Pulumi Insights provides visibility and misconfiguration analysis.
Pulumi Policies provide AI-specific guardrails in code, cost detection, and automated compliance protections.
Infrastructure as Code is becoming the foundation for scaling reliably across all environments, and organizations are increasingly adopting IaC in general-purpose languages.
Modern IaC (Pulumi) integrates with third-party data platforms and messaging systems including CockroachDB, Confluent Cloud, and Kafka.
Pulumi Insights Discovery (pulumi.com/docs/insights/discovery/) improves cloud resource efficiency and visibility.
Pulumi Policy as Code (pulumi.com/docs/insights/policy/) automatically enforces guardrails, cost controls, and regulatory requirements.
Modern IaC enables intelligent automation from unit and integration tests to auto-remediation policies and policy-driven approvals.
Pulumi Policies (per pulumi.com/blog/policy-next-gen/) incorporate AI-driven optimization and insights that detect misconfigurations, analyze usage patterns, and generate infrastructure updates.
IaC has become critical for achieving secure, repeatable, high-velocity operations across every environment.
Gartner (press release 2026-03-17) predicts that by 2028 over 50% of enterprises will use AI security platforms to secure third-party AI service usage and protect custom-built AI applications.
Gartner projects total spending on securing AI to reach roughly $4.8 billion in 2027.
DevSecOps is entering a new, AI-integrated era.
Pulumi offers AI-powered remediation capabilities (pulumi.com/product/insights-governance/#video).
Carlie Idoine is a VP Analyst at Gartner and made the quoted remarks at the Gartner Data & Analytics Summit in Sydney.

Carlie Idoine (Gartner) said: '[AI]... it doesn't deliver value on its own – AI needs to be tightly aligned with data, analytics, and governance to enable intelligent, adaptive decisions and actions across the organization.'
Pulumi provides infrastructure as code, reusable components, and policy guardrails for delivering across every cloud and AI workload.

According to Gartner (gartner.com 'What is platform engineering' article), by 2026, 80% of large software engineering organizations will establish platform engineering teams as internal providers of reusable services, components, and tools for application delivery.
As of this post's update (2026-09-15), Gartner's 2026 target year for platform engineering adoption has arrived.
CNCF published a Q1 2026 Technology Radar report with SlashData, announced 2026-03-24, on platform engineering tools maturing as organizations prepare for AI-driven infrastructure.
The CNCF/SlashData Q1 2026 Technology Radar report found 28% of surveyed organizations already have a dedicated platform engineering team.
The CNCF/SlashData Q1 2026 Technology Radar report found 35% of surveyed organizations are running a hybrid platform that combines existing developer platforms with specialized AI tooling.

Chris Aniszczyk said, in the CNCF Q1 2026 report announcement: 'Cloud native platforms have reached a point where developers are not just experimenting but standardizing on CNCF projects that make software delivery reliable at scale.'

Chris Aniszczyk said: 'What's especially notable about this research is how organizations are extending those same platforms to support AI workloads, showing how cloud native is the base layer of powering the next era of applications.'
Chris Aniszczyk is CTO of CNCF.
Mid-size to large companies continue to invest in platform engineering practices, with large tech companies as first adopters.
Developer Experience is abbreviated DX and is sometimes referred to as DE or DevEx.
The Pulumi blog posts platform-engineering-pillars-3, announcing-pulumi-idp, and developer-experience-business-critical exist at the linked URLs.
The image https://www.pulumi.com/blog/developer-portal-platform-teams/platform-teams.png exists and is credited to Pulumi.
IDPs are reshaping how developers interact with cloud infrastructure, bringing together platform engineering, automation, and AI platform engineering practices.
Gartner (gartner.com 'AI for infrastructure operations' article) predicts agentic AI deployment in IT operations grows from under 5% in 2025 to 70% by 2029.
Gartner predicts human-in-the-loop requirements in IT operations workflows fall from 95% in 2025 to 40% by 2028.
Pulumi's 2026 State of Agentic Infrastructure survey shows an agentic-operations shift starting inside real teams and a gap between sentiment and practice.
Pulumi's 2026 survey found 82% of respondents agree that AI and agents will meaningfully change how they write infrastructure within 12 months.
Pulumi's 2026 survey found 63% of respondents say they trust agents to make production changes.
Pulumi's 2026 survey found manual approval of agent-made infrastructure changes remains close to universal today.
Pulumi's 2026 survey report describes the trust-vs-approval gap as stated trust outrunning real guardrails.
Pulumi's 2026 survey found the share of teams expecting agents to generate half or more of their infrastructure code rises from 45% today to 52% within six months.
Pulumi Neo (pulumi.com/product/neo/) proposes infrastructure changes, runs previews, and executes approved updates with policy guardrails in place, keeping a human accountable for approval.

Pulumi's blog post 'The Agentic Infrastructure Era' (pulumi.com/blog/the-agentic-infrastructure-era/) argues AIOps is headed toward a supervised agentic operating model rather than faster dashboards and alerting alone.
What has changed in AIOps for 2027 is that observability/automation/analytics signals increasingly feed an agent empowered to act on them, with a person reviewing the result.
Kubernetes will continue its ascent in 2027.
Mordor Intelligence values the global Kubernetes market at USD 3.13 billion in 2026.
Mordor Intelligence projects the global Kubernetes market to reach USD 8.41 billion by 2031.
Mordor Intelligence's Kubernetes market forecast (USD 3.13B in 2026 to USD 8.41B in 2031) corresponds to a 21.85% CAGR.
CNCF published a Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report (PDF at cncf.io, uploaded Nov 2025).
The CNCF Q3 2025 State of Cloud Native Development report puts cloud-native adoption among professional ML/AI developers at 41%.
The CNCF Q3 2025 report says 30% of backend developers now use Kubernetes directly.
Per the CNCF report, direct Kubernetes usage among backend developers peaked at 36% in Q3 2023.
The CNCF Q3 2025 report attributes the slow decline in direct Kubernetes usage among backend developers to the technology's growing maturity.

The Pulumi blog posts beyond-yaml-kubernetes-2026-automation-era (with anchor #the-2026-convergence-of-ai-platforms-and-policy-in-kubernetes) and best-kubernetes-iac-tools-2026 (a comparison of Kubernetes IaC tools) exist.

LLM- and GPU-powered inference workloads now require low-latency execution closer to the user, pushing organizations toward orchestration layers spanning edge and core clusters with Kubernetes as the common control plane.
Kubernetes is evolving to support AI through GPU-aware scheduling and more advanced workload orchestration.

Kubernetes will remain a strategic foundation, but operating it effectively now depends on robust automation, strong security controls, standardized delivery models, and platform engineering rather than raw YAML.
GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, and Cursor are AI-powered coding assistants.
AI-powered coding assistants have moved from novelty to everyday tooling for a large share of enterprise software teams, and this shift is now reaching infrastructure code.
The 'value of AI code assistants' figure (ai_code_assistants_value.png) is credited to Gartner.
According to Gartner (press release 2024-04-11), by 2028, 75% of enterprise software engineers will use dedicated AI code assistants.
According to Gartner, 63% of organizations are currently piloting, deploying, or beginning to use AI code assistants (framed as current in a post updated 2026-09-15, citing a 2024-04-11 release).
A revision of the Model Context Protocol was released in July 2026 (MCP blog post dated 2026-07-28).
The Model Context Protocol maintainers described the July 2026 revision as the largest revision of the protocol to date.
AWS shipped a general-availability MCP server for its Agent Toolkit (AWS What's New, May 2026).
Mirantis's Lens (a Kubernetes tooling product) has launched a built-in MCP server connecting AI coding assistants to Kubernetes.
Enterprise expectations for AI assistants are rising: they must understand infrastructure state, configurations, and security posture and be able to act directly on infrastructure.
Pulumi Agent Skills (pulumi.com/blog/pulumi-agent-skills/) is one of the newest Pulumi releases, a collection of infrastructure expertise packaged for use in AI coding assistants.
Pulumi Agent Skills work with Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI, teaching them to reason about Pulumi projects.
Pulumi Agent Skills reduce hallucination and improve AI assistant outputs based on real infrastructure conventions and practices.
Pulumi offers a Remote MCP Server (pulumi.com/blog/remote-mcp-server/) providing AI assistants access to infrastructure.
AI code assistants are no longer experimental and are fast becoming a competitive advantage in cloud software development.
Cloud infrastructure is entering its most transformative era since the rise of Kubernetes, with AI now setting the organizing principle for cloud strategy.

AIOps and intelligent automation are becoming standard for scaling modern cloud systems, alongside AI-native architectures, IaC as backbone, platform engineering, integrated security, Kubernetes for AI, and multi-cloud ecosystems.
Modern IaC, unified governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks are all core capabilities of the Pulumi Cloud platform.

Organizations that invest now in modern IaC, governance, reusable components, and policy frameworks will be positioned to lead in an AI-first world, and the gap versus non-modernizers will widen rapidly in 2027 and beyond.
The Pulumi getting-started page /docs/get-started/ exists (CTA target).

Engineering teams must adapt with IaC-driven automation, reusable patterns, and policy controls, and must deploy workloads across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, on-prem, and edge with consistent security, compliance, and configuration as AI and regulatory requirements grow.
